title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Average Salary Brisbane Guide
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes average salary Brisbane context, tax, super, and minimum wage details.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the national full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Remember that this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the average salary in Brisbane?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics does not publish a specific average salary for Brisbane. The national full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. For a 38-hour week, that equates to roughly $54.83 per hour. However, this is a national average and may not reflect your specific job or industry. For a more tailored figure, check industry awards or your employer's pay rates.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For example, if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for your employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’re an employee or contractor in Australia, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and comparing job offers. This guide walks you through the simple formula, explains the role of a 38-hour week, and covers tax, super, and the **average salary Brisbane** context. We’ll also clarify the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading.

## The Basic Formula

The standard conversion from hourly to annual pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week for 52 weeks a year. It does not account for unpaid leave, overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full-time employee working a 38-hour week, the formula becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross would be:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44

If you’re paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For the minimum wage, a fortnight’s gross pay is $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80.

## The 38-Hour Week and Fortnight

Australia’s standard full-time week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. Many awards and agreements use this as the base. When converting your hourly rate, always confirm your ordinary hours. If you work 40 hours, use 40 in the formula. The fortnightly equivalent is your weekly pay doubled, which helps when budgeting for bills that come every two weeks.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Most industries have award rates that are higher. For example, a hospitality award might pay $28 per hour for a Level 1 employee. Always check the relevant award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) to find your correct rate.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [the timesheet](/), you can tick a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. **Do not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading; enter the base rate and let the tool add it.

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. For a single person earning $80,000, the tax would be approximately $16,867 plus $1,600 Medicare levy, leaving a take-home of about $61,533. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator for a more precise calculation.

## Superannuation

Super is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer must contribute $9,600 to your super fund. This is separate from your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Average Salary Brisbane Context

When people search for **average salary Brisbane**, they often want a benchmark for their industry or role. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes national figures, not city-specific ones. The latest ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week nationally. That’s about $108,352 per year for a 38-hour week. However, this is an **average** across all full-time adults, not a median for a specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your occupation, experience, and location. For Brisbane, the average might be slightly different due to industry mix, but the ABS does not release a separate figure. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference to compare with national averages.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Remember to use the correct hours (often 38), consider casual loading if applicable, and understand that tax and super are separate. The **average salary Brisbane** is a useful benchmark, but always check your award or agreement for your specific rate. For a quick calculation, visit our [the timesheet](/).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
